semantic_adjudication.reason: The NL requires the Approaching state to 'send the Send signal' - this is an output effect produced by the state. The PlantUML source at line 14 uses 'exit/Send' as a transition label. In the FCSTM, the entire label is preserved as one opaque event 'exit_Send' (line 6), making it an input trigger that the transition waits for, rather than an output effect the state produces. The structural distinction is critical: a trigger is an external event that must be received to fire the transition, while an effect is produced by the system as a result of the transition. decisions.reason: The NL requires the state to 'send' the Obstacle Detected signal, which is an output effect. The FCSTM state EmergencyStopping has no entry or do effect. decisions.basis: NL9 requirement quote from dossier, FCSTM state:Approaching:line:13 with no effect fields, transition:line:18 trigger='exit_Send' effect='R45RouteToken = 7', source_inventory tr_0007 event='exit/Send' as trigger not effect

decisions.basis: NL9 requirement quote from dossier, PlantUML source line 14 'Approaching --> InMotion:exit/Send', FCSTM event:exit_Send:line:6 as opaque trigger, transition:line:18 and transition:line:29, R45.DEBT.opaque_transition_label_semantics lowering rule

The PlantUML source at line 14 uses 'exit/Send' as a transition label. In the FCSTM, the entire label is preserved as one opaque event 'exit_Send' (line 6), making it an input trigger that the transition waits for, rather than an output effect the state produces. decisions.violated_obligation: The 'Send' signal must be encoded as a state exit action (output effect) of the Approaching state, not as an opaque input trigger on the Approaching-to-InMotion transition.

issues.reason: The NL explicitly requires an entry action 'Accelerate' on the Accelerating substate (phase=entry from the 'Entry/Accelerate' marker). The FCSTM has no formal action on this state or on its initial entry transition. All three S4 inputs are available: state=Accelerating, phase=entry, action=Accelerate.
issues.requirement_quote: The system enters the Accelerating substate when motion begins, marked by the "Entry/Accelerate" action.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The PlantUML state description 'Accelerating' could be interpreted as implicitly indicating the action; however, the NL explicitly specifies 'Entry/Accelerate' as a formal action marker, and the FCSTM has no typed entry action on this state.
issues.title: Accelerating substate lacks the required entry action 'Accelerate'

issues.basis: NL9 segment text; FCSTM transition:line:18 (triggers=[exit_Send], effects=[R45RouteToken = 7]); FCSTM state:Approaching:line:13 (no effect); exact_source_inventory transition tr_0007 (event='exit/Send').
issues.expected: The Approaching substate sends the 'Send' signal as an output effect.
issues.observed: The FCSTM state Approaching (line 13) has no effect field. The 'Send' appears only as part of the trigger name exit_Send on the exit transition:line:18 (Approaching -> [*]). The actual effect on that transition is 'R45RouteToken = 7', a compiler-generated variable assignment, not a signal emission. No effect on the state or any transition encodes sending the 'Send' signal.
issues.reason: The NL requires the Approaching substate to send the 'Send' signal. In the FCSTM, 'Send' appears only in the trigger name (exit_Send) of the exit transition, not as an effect. The transition's actual effect is a compiler-generated variable assignment (R45RouteToken = 7). No state-level or transition-level effect encodes signal emission.
issues.requirement_quote: In the Approaching substate, the system sends the "Send" signal and continues to approach the destination.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source models 'exit/Send' as the event label on the exit transition from Approaching to InMotion, which could be interpreted as the signal being sent during the exit; however, in the FCSTM this is encoded as a trigger (input event name) not an effect (output signal), so the state does not actively emit the signal.
issues.title: Approaching substate lacks the required 'Send' signal-sending effect

issues.basis: NL9 segment text; FCSTM state:Approaching:line:13 (body text only, no action); reference_inspection_facts abstract_action_inventory (count 0).
issues.expected: The Approaching substate has a continuous (do) action of approaching the destination.
issues.observed: The FCSTM state Approaching (line 13) has no formal action. Its body contains only the description text 'Approaching'. No do-action or continuous behavior is encoded on this state. The reference inspection facts confirm zero actions in the abstract action inventory.
issues.reason: The NL requires the Approaching substate to have a continuous action of approaching the destination. The FCSTM has no formal action on this state. Since no explicit lifecycle phase is provided in the binding hints (the NL says 'continues to' which implies do, but the contract extraction did not supply a phase hint), S4 cannot be applied.
issues.requirement_quote: In the Approaching substate, the system sends the "Send" signal and continues to approach the destination.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The state description 'Approaching' could be interpreted as implicitly indicating the continuous behavior; however, the NL explicitly states 'continues to approach the destination' as a distinct action from the signal-sending effect, and no formal action is present in the FCSTM.
issues.title: Approaching substate lacks the required continuous action 'approach the destination'
